data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's central thesis is that within a single evaluation one 'cannot definitively distinguish' genuine reliability gain from mere compliance tracking, because single-evaluation evidence is structurally insufficient. Yet SRC_001's own counterconditions list exactly the within-single-evidence designs that accomplish this: (a) a single evaluation can include 'adversarial items specifically designed to break surface correlations,' and SRC_001 concedes this 'could suffice within one evaluation'; and (b) if 'the checklist is provably causally complete (deductive),' the distinction collapses within that evaluation. The problem explicitly asks to '[i]dentify what evidence within a single evaluation would distinguish' the two, not to argue the distinction is impossible. SRC_001 is therefore self-refuting: it denies the possibility while listing feasible within-evaluation mechanisms that satisfy the problem's demand.
